concerns.concern: The headline claim of improved performance rests on effective conductivity, which is not a thermoelectric figure of merit. Using the paper's own numbers, conventional Pt/YIG single-crystal devices reach a power factor comparable to or larger than the best composite, so trans-scaling is not shown to improve conversion.
concerns.quote: The manuscript therefore does not show that trans-scaling improves the conversion performance it was designed to improve.

concerns.concern: XRD and magnetometry cannot rule out a sub-percent ferromagnetic metallic phase whose anomalous Nernst effect could produce the ~10 nV/K signal. Possible sources are Fe-Pt interdiffusion under high-pressure shear and Co transfer from the tungsten-carbide die.
concerns.quote: XRD detection limits (~1–5 wt%) cannot exclude a sub-percent, possibly percolating or interfacial ferromagnetic metallic phase.

concerns.concern: Decisive controls for an SSE origin are missing: Pt on a non-magnetic garnet, spin-Hall-angle sign reversal or null tests with W/Ta/Cu, high-field magnon suppression, temperature dependence, and null geometries.
concerns.quote: A Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet (GGG or YAG powder) processed identically.

concerns.concern: The volumetric SSE mechanism is asserted without any quantitative model. No estimate accounts for orientation averaging, intra-shell circulating currents, network shunting, or known Pt/YIG parameters, so readers cannot judge whether ~10 nV/K is consistent with SSE.
concerns.quote: The "volumetric" SSE mechanism is asserted, not demonstrated or modelled.

concerns.concern: No conventional reference sample, such as Pt on a YIG single crystal or on a sintered YIG slab, was measured in the same setup. Cross-laboratory comparison of the Seebeck coefficient is therefore unreliable.
concerns.quote: Without it, cross-laboratory comparison of SSSE is unreliable, because heat-bath interfaces and ∇T definitions differ.

concerns.concern: The isotropy comparison uses two different heat-bath and contact schemes, and the temperature gradient was inferred from the bath rather than measured on the sample. The near-identical values in the two configurations may therefore be coincidental.
concerns.quote: The agreement of 14.8 vs 14.4 nV/K may therefore be partly coincidental.

concerns.concern: Directional isotropy is an expected geometric consequence of randomly oriented interfaces. It would equally arise from ANE of an isotropically distributed ferromagnetic contaminant, so it is not discriminating evidence for SSE.
concerns.quote: it is not discriminating evidence (the authors partially acknowledge this).

concerns.concern: All samples come from a single batch, with one sample per condition, no error bars and no repeats. Density also co-varies with processing. The reported ~2× differences and the 630% power-factor enhancement are therefore not statistically established or disentangled.
concerns.quote: The ~2× differences in SSSE and the "630%" PF enhancement are therefore not statistically established.

concerns.concern: Sample trends are unexplained. The Seebeck coefficient anti-correlates with conductivity, and the product σeff·SSSE scales mainly with Pt thickness, which points to shunting-controlled behavior that should be analyzed with σxy-type quantities.
concerns.quote: This points to shunting-controlled behavior.

concerns.concern: The Hall test excluding anomalous Hall contributions is only qualitative. It gives no noise floor or upper bound on ANE, was done in a different apparatus at 100 mA with possible Joule heating, and shows no current-reversal data. The absence of known SMR-type signals suggests insufficient sensitivity.
concerns.quote: No bound is given on an anomalous-Hall component relative to noise, and there is no conversion to an upper limit on ANE

concerns.concern: Pt volume fraction, actual shell thickness and connectivity are unknown for the 15 and 30 nm samples. These were labelled only from deposition time and were not verified by TEM after compaction.
concerns.quote: Pt volume fraction, actual shell thickness, and connectivity are unknown for the 15/30 nm samples

concerns.concern: The YIG particle size distribution after crushing is not reported, even though grain size relative to the magnon diffusion length is central to the concept.
concerns.quote: The YIG particle size distribution after crushing is not reported

concerns.concern: The field dependence of the signal is not compared with demagnetization-corrected magnetization along the same axis. In the rotated configuration the signal keeps rising up to ~5 kOe, unlike M(H).
concerns.quote: The Hx-∇zT curve in Fig. 3e keeps increasing up to ~5 kOe, unlike M(H).

concerns.concern: No zT, power density, or maximum output power under matched load is reported. The estimated zT (~8×10⁻¹¹) should be stated and discussed honestly.
concerns.quote: No zT, power density, or maximum output power under matched load is given.

concerns.concern: Porosity of 25–33% may interrupt the Pt shells. Pt-rich aggregates in the EDX map could indicate smearing or agglomeration during pressing rather than conformal shells.
concerns.quote: The EDX map shows Pt-rich aggregates that could indicate smearing or agglomeration during pressing rather than conformal shells.

concerns.concern: The magnetization argument is not quantitative. The saturation magnetization drop is about the same for 15 and 30 nm Pt even though the Pt mass fraction should differ by ~2×, which could mask a small ferromagnetic contribution.
concerns.quote: The magnetization argument is not quantitative.

concerns.concern: The sign of the signal is not checked against the established Pt/YIG convention.
concerns.quote: The signal sign is not checked against the established Pt/YIG convention.

concerns.concern: The physics novelty is modest compared with prior bulk SSE nanocomposites. The work reads as a materials and process demonstration rather than a physics advance suited to a top-tier physics journal.
concerns.quote: it reads more like a materials and process demonstration than a physics advance of the breadth expected by a top-tier physics journal.

concerns.concern: No systematic series in grain size, Pt thickness and density are provided. These are needed to test whether the signal responds to grain size around the magnon diffusion length, as volumetric magnon utilization would imply.
concerns.quote: If volumetric magnon utilization is real, the signal should respond to grain size around λm.

concerns.concern: The claim that 15 and 30 nm Pt thicknesses well above the spin diffusion length ensure clear observation is conceptually reversed, because thicker normal metal increases shunting and reduces the field.
concerns.quote: the claim that 15 nm and 30 nm are "well above λs, ensuring clear observation" is conceptually reversed

concerns.concern: Comparisons with undoped Si/Ge and the bad-metal regime are irrelevant to transverse thermoelectric performance. The comparison with thin-film σeff depends on an arbitrary substrate thickness.
concerns.quote: The comparison with thin-film σeff depends on an arbitrary substrate thickness.

concerns.concern: The exclusion of α-Fe2O3/YFeO3 contributions is argued only qualitatively, after conceding that XRD cannot distinguish them.
concerns.quote: The α-Fe2O3/YFeO3 exclusion is argued only qualitatively, after conceding that XRD cannot distinguish them.

concerns.concern: The thermal conductivity data need validation. Laser-flash diffusivity on porous, metal-networked samples gives κ well below porosity models, and polycrystalline κ is taken from literature rather than measured on a pressed pure-YIG reference.
concerns.quote: Polycrystalline κ is taken from the literature rather than measured on a pressed pure-YIG reference.

concerns.concern: Magnetization units appear inconsistent: Fig. 3f shows ~0.02–0.03 emu/g while the text quotes 37.9 emu/g. The latter is also closer to YIG's low-temperature Ms than its room-temperature value.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3f shows ~0.02–0.03 "emu/g", while the text quotes 37.9 emu/g.

concerns.concern: The terms "nanostructured" (the grains are µm-scale) and "sintering at room temperature" (actually cold compaction) are overstated.
concerns.quote: "Nanostructured" (the grains are µm-scale) and "sintering at room temperature" (this is cold compaction) are also overstated.

concerns.concern: Pt cost and mass fraction (~10 wt%) are not discussed in the context of the claimed scalability.
concerns.quote: Also discuss Pt cost and mass fraction (~10 wt% estimated) in the context of "scalability".

concerns.concern: Only one sample was measured in the rotated geometry. The reviewer asks that isotropy be demonstrated on the same cubic specimen in three orientations.
concerns.quote: Only one sample was measured in the rotated geometry.

concerns.concern: The text compares the second configuration with "Hx-∇zT" (Fig. 3c), which appears to be a typo for Hz-∇xT.
concerns.quote: the second configuration is compared with "Hx-∇zT" (Fig. 3c), which appears to be a typo for Hz-∇xT.

concerns.concern: Robust mechanical integrity is claimed without any mechanical testing.
concerns.quote: "Robust mechanical integrity" is claimed without any mechanical testing.

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength is given inconsistently in Methods and the SI.
concerns.quote: Cu-Kα wavelengths differ (0.15406 nm in Methods vs 0.15418 nm in the SI).

concerns.concern: The FePt reference card is listed with the same PDF number as Y2O3.
concerns.quote: The FePt card is listed with the same PDF number as Y2O3 (#43-0661).

concerns.concern: The XRD figures are cross-referenced as "Fig. S2" in Note S2.
concerns.quote: XRD figures are cross-referenced as "Fig. S2" in Note S2.

concerns.concern: The name "Galosov" is misspelled and should be Golosov.
concerns.quote: "Galosov" is misspelled (should be Golosov).
